description: Command-line tool to view and configure Windows Advanced Audit Policy for security event logging.
prerequisites: Windows Vista or later for Advanced Audit Policy
PowerShell recommended for CSV parsing and automation

flags.purpose: Displays current audit policy for all top-level categories.
flags.outputs: Readable table of audit success/failure settings per category.
flags.security_use_case: Baseline audit coverage review for compliance and SOC visibility.
flags.threat_detected: Missing audit categories allowing attacker activity without logs.
flags.risk_if_misused: None (read-only). Does not show granular subcategory detail.

flags.purpose: Retrieves audit policy for granular subcategories.
flags.outputs: Success/Failure audit state for specific sensitive operations.
flags.security_use_case: Verify auditing for privilege use, process creation, registry, and credential validation.
flags.threat_detected: Privilege abuse or credential attacks occurring without logs.
flags.safe_followup: Enable success and failure auditing using /set.

flags.purpose: Enables or disables auditing for categories/subcategories.
flags.outputs: Modified audit configuration reflected in Security Event Log behavior.
flags.security_use_case: Enable failure auditing to detect brute-force and abuse attempts.
flags.threat_detected: Attack activity not logged due to disabled audit policies.
flags.risk_if_misused: May generate excessive logs; requires admin rights; potential performance/log overflow.
flags.safe_followup: Configure log retention, forwarding to SIEM, and monitor event volume.

flags.purpose: Backs up current audit policy to CSV.
flags.outputs: CSV file containing full audit configuration.
flags.security_use_case: Create baseline before changes and for compliance documentation.
flags.risk_if_misused: Backup file must be protected from tampering.
flags.safe_followup: Store backup securely; compare with /get outputs regularly.

flags.outputs: Audit configuration reverted to backup state.
flags.security_use_case: Recover from misconfiguration or post-incident recovery.
flags.threat_detected: Restoring maliciously modified backup or wrong host policy.
flags.risk_if_misused: Must verify backup integrity and host relevance.
flags.safe_followup: Validate with /get after restore; test in non-production.

flags.outputs: Full list of advanced audit subcategories.

flags.purpose: Resets audit policy to system defaults.
flags.security_use_case: Only when baseline is unknown and full reset is required.
flags.threat_detected: Destroys forensic audit trail if used during investigation.
flags.risk_if_misused: Highly dangerous; removes all custom auditing.
flags.safe_followup: Always perform /backup before; avoid in live environments.

powerful_combinations.why_powerful: Converts audit category output into structured CSV for automation and reporting.
powerful_combinations.security_context: SOC baseline audit review and compliance reporting.

powerful_combinations.command: auditpol /get /subcategory:"Credential Validation","User Account Management","Security Group Management","Audit Policy Change" /r
powerful_combinations.why_powerful: Focuses on the most attack-relevant subcategories for account compromise detection.
powerful_combinations.security_context: Detect credential theft, group privilege abuse, and audit tampering.

powerful_combinations.command: auditpol /backup /file:"$env:COMPUTERNAME-audit-$(Get-Date -Format yyyyMMdd).csv"; auditpol /get /category:* /r | ConvertFrom-Csv | Export-Csv all_audit_policies.csv -NoTypeInformation
powerful_combinations.why_powerful: Creates timestamped backup and full export for forensic readiness.
powerful_combinations.security_context: Disaster recovery, compliance evidence, and incident preparation.
